newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Vedior float spiced up with London listing.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Vedior float spiced up with London listing.

text.p: Dutch retail and services group Vendex International on Monday confirmed plans to spin-off its Vedior services arm in a complex process that breaks new ground for listed companies in the Netherlands.
But Vendex spiced up the spin-off proposal announced previously, which requires Dutch government approval, by adding a London listing of the new company and beefing up an associated capital raising.

Analysts said Vendex had picked its timing sweetly as sharemarkets were buoyant and profits from Vedior's main business, French temporary employment agency BIS, were improving. "It's a good market to be in," said John Ebbing of Bangert Pontier.
Investors reacted positively to the latest news, marking up Vendex shares by 1.40 guilders to 96.80 at 1340 GMT.
Vendex earlier announced it would list Vedior NV on the Amsterdam and London stock exchanges in June.
"The bourse introduction will occur through the placing of ordinary shares in Vedior NV worth between 600 million and 650 million guilders ($314 million-$340 million)," Vendex said.
In April, the Dutch company said it planned to raise 600 million guilders through an initial public offering (IPO) of Vedior on the Amsterdam bourse.
Ebbing said he expected the proceeds of the flotation to be at the upper end of the 600-650 million guilder range.
Marketing and bookbuilding for the placing are expected to take place in the second half of May, while listing on the Amsterdam bourse is expected in the first two weeks of June.
Morgan Stanley & Co International Ltd will be global coordinator to the placing.
Analysts were positive that the new company, which is also involved in cleaning and security, would be listed in London, where it will get more exposure among international investors.
But they wondered why Vendex did not seek a listing on the Paris bourse, in view of the fact that Vedior draws 60 percent of its revenue from France.
"Maybe it will come later," Ebbing said.
Vendex has not yet disclosed what proportion of Vedior it is floating off through the IPO, saying only it would be a minority stake, but analysts estimated the share at about 25 percent.
MeesPierson analyst Jurgen Veenker ascribed a value of about 2.5 billion guilders to Vedior, adding the Dutch share market had risen considerably since last month.
"Temporary employment agencies have moved in line with, or slightly better than, the market," he said.
Vendex has said shareholders of the 'old' Vendex would receive the remaining Vedior shares as soon as possible after the float with the split-up to be finalised early in 1998.
Analysts said negotiations with the Ministry of Finance were dragging on because of the complex nature of the process, which requires changes in the law on the split-up of legal entities.
One analyst said this would be the first time a listed Dutch company had decided to de-merge in this way, giving Vendex shareholders shares in a pure retailer and a services group.
Vendex, the second largest Dutch retailer and owner of the upmarket Vroom & Dreesmann department store chain, listed on the Amsterdam exchange in June 1995.
One of the largest privately-held Dutch companies until its listing, it dates back to 1882 when the first V&D store opened in Amsterdam.
It has since expanded into services, including the $473 million takeover of BIS in January this year. ($=1.91 guilders)
